items.stem: A U.S. retailer launches an online loyalty program that profiles consumers. Which characteristic best describes the U.S. privacy legal framework it must navigate?

options.text: A sectoral and state-by-state patchwork rather than a single omnibus federal law
options.rationale: Correct: U.S. privacy law is largely sectoral and state-driven rather than one omnibus federal statute.

options.text: A single comprehensive federal privacy statute covering all sectors
options.rationale: The U.S. has no single omnibus federal privacy law covering all sectors.
State privacy laws differ substantially from one another.

options.text: No applicable privacy obligations at all
options.rationale: Numerous sectoral and state obligations apply.

items.explanation: Correct: U.S. privacy law is largely sectoral and state-driven rather than one omnibus federal statute.

options.rationale: Correct: GLBA governs privacy and safeguarding of consumer financial information at financial institutions.
The FLSA governs wages and hours, not financial privacy.
This is an environmental statute, unrelated to privacy.
This is competition law, not financial privacy.

items.stem: Select TWO common consumer rights featured in recent U.S. state comprehensive privacy laws. (Select TWO.)

options.text: The right to access personal data a business holds about the consumer
options.rationale: Correct: access/know is a common right in state comprehensive laws.

options.text: The right to delete personal data, subject to exceptions
options.rationale: Correct: deletion is a common state-law consumer right, subject to exceptions.

options.text: The right to a guaranteed paid vacation
options.rationale: That is an employment-benefit matter, not a privacy right.

options.text: The right to free broadband from the state
options.rationale: No such privacy right exists in these laws.

options.text: The right to set national monetary policy
options.rationale: This is unrelated to consumer privacy rights.

items.explanation: Correct: access/know is a common right in state comprehensive laws.
